claim: Stablecoin adoption is forecast to be fastest in cross-border and high-value B2B flows, not consumer retail, because that is where cost/speed benefits are clearest.
stance_target: near-term consumer-retail stablecoin disruption of Apple Pay
scope_conditions: Third Bridge expert-network calls, as of ~Jan 2026
quoted_support: Adoption is forecast to be fastest in cross-border and high-value B2B flows...where stablecoins can materially cut costs and settlement times and deliver clearer benefits than in consumer retail.

claim: The greatest risk to card networks is merchant-led adoption by large platforms (Amazon, Walmart, Shopify) that have incentives to route payments over lower-cost stablecoin rails.
stance_target: strongest version of reader's prior on payment disruption
quoted_support: The greatest risk to Visa and Mastercard, our experts say, is merchant-led adoption, as platforms such as Amazon, Walmart, and Shopify have strong incentives to route payments over lower-cost stablecoin rails and reshape checkout economics.

claim: A Visa expert on a July 2025 call downplayed stablecoin threat magnitude, saying real-world impact is 'less' than commonly suggested even where credible.
stance_target: reader's prior of imminent large-scale disruption
scope_conditions: single expert quote, July 2025 Visa cross-border outlook call
quoted_support: There's certainly the possibility of stablecoins being a meaningful threat and reducing Visa's network volumes, particularly as it applies to cross-border, but I think that it's really less of an impact than some folks would have you suggest.

claim: Card networks are not being disintermediated; they are absorbing stablecoins via multi-rail 'network-of-networks' strategies (Visa Conecta, VTAP) with value-added-services revenue growing 20%+ annually.
quoted_support: Our experts estimated that VAS revenue will continue to grow 20%+ annually, with consulting, fraud, and tokenization emerging as the largest contributors.

claim: Visa and Mastercard stock have lagged the S&P 500 over the trailing three years as of January 13, 2026, reflecting market-priced disruption risk.
stance_target: market perceives stablecoin risk as real, even if not yet realized in revenue
scope_conditions: trailing 3-year total return, as of Jan 13 2026
quoted_support: Visa up 54%, Mastercard up 49%, and the S&P 500 up 75%.
